thread:
maria-nguyen: FYI CI scan just flagged something odd on the 2026.03 release build — license + signing/attestation warnings.
sec-scan-bot: [automated] build-2026.03: SBOM policy: non-permissive license detected (GPL-3.0-or-later) in transitive dep 'libhashx@2.1.0'. Artifact signing: KMS key last rotated 2018-06, attestation missing. Severity: high.
joel-patel: Can you paste the SBOM edges and the exact artifact id?
maria-nguyen: Artifact: registry.redwood-inference/internal/runtime:2026.03. sha256:af3d...c4b (shortened). SBOM snippet: 
```
# from sbom.json
- libfoo@1.4.2 -> libhashx@2.1.0 (license: GPL-3.0-or-later)
- libhashx@2.1.0 (source: github.com/thirdparty/hashx)
```
maria-nguyen: The signing metadata in the artifact manifest shows signing-key-id: kms-prod-legacy-01 and there is no SLSA attestation recorded in our attestations bucket.
samir: Oof. Two things: 1) GPL transitive may be fine for internal infra but we must confirm distribution policy for the runtime image. 2) KMS key age + missing attestation is concerning — could be mis-signed or a CI misconfiguration.
leah: Immediate plan: pause pushes for this CI job, quarantine the artifact in registry, set deploy gate to fallback image. Who can flip RBAC to stop the CI service account from writing to the registry?
joel-patel: I can. I'll add a temporary deny on principal `ci-runner@redwood-inference` for `storage.objects.create`/`ecr:PutImage` depending on registry. Will also create an allow for a maintainer group to push hotfix images.
maria-nguyen: Command for GCS-backed registry (example):
```
# revoke write for CI principal (gcloud example)
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \
  --member="serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/storage.objectViewer" 
# remove writer role, keep viewer
```
maria-nguyen: For AWS ECR equivalent we'd update the repository policy to deny PutImage for that principal.
ops-bot: NOTE: registry quarantine invoked for artifact sha256:af3d...c4b — pull disabled.
sec-scan-bot: Added tag `quarantined` to artifact and blocked promotion pipelines.
samir: Next: rotate/signing key. Options: rotate kms-prod-legacy-01, but that won't retroactively validate old artifacts. We should: 1) rotate the key, 2) require re-sign + attestation before promoting, 3) rebuild artifact from commit and verify SBOM and attestation.
leah: Agree. I'll start a rebuild with `libhashx` pinned to patched fork (legal okayed?) — legal already pinged and says transitive GPL flagged, they're ok if runtime isn’t redistributed externally but want us to avoid mixing in customer-facing binaries. For safety we should remove dependency or replace with MIT-licensed fork.
maria-nguyen: Quick rebuild plan: create a canary image `runtime:2026.03-canary-1` that excludes libhashx (or vendor patched MIT fork) -> run integration smoke -> route 5% traffic to canary. If good, promote.
joel-patel: I'll open a short-lived RBAC exception for maintainers to push the canary. Then I'll revoke after promotion.
leah: For KMS: suggested commands (generic):
```
# rotate key (pseudo)
kms-cli rotate-key --key-id kms-prod-legacy-01 --new-key-label kms-prod-2026-rot1
# create signed-attestation
attest-cli create --artifact sha256:af3d...c4b --key kms-prod-2026-rot1 --predicate-file sbom-attest.json
```
maria-nguyen: Note — we must not delete the legacy key until we can validate signatures or archive old signed artifacts. Schedule deletion only after incident review.
ops-bot: I've created ticket INF-1125 (quarantine + rebuild + kms rotation + legal review). Assigned: maria-nguyen, joel-patel, samir, leah.
samir: Action checklist (short):
- [x] Quarantine artifact in registry
- [x] Pause promotion pipelines
- [x] Notify legal for license risk (leah did)
- [ ] Rebuild without libhashx or use MIT fork
- [ ] Produce SLSA attestation and re-sign with rotated KMS key
- [ ] Smoke tests + canary 5%
- [ ] Roll forward and revoke RBAC exception
- [ ] Post-incident writeup + update SBOM policy docs
maria-nguyen: ETA on rebuild + attestation? I can get a reproducible build + unit/integration tests in ~3 hours if the team allocates a runner.
joel-patel: Allocated a high-priority runner, starting now. I'll also push RBAC change and revoke in two steps (open window for canary push).
leah: Legal will follow in INF-1125 with notes; contact point: legal@redwood. They want the exact SBOM path and license file.
maria-nguyen: I'll attach SBOM + signing metadata to the ticket and put a link to the quarantined artifact.
sec-scan-bot: Will re-scan rebuilt artifacts automatically once pushed to `canary` tag.
maria-nguyen: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the coord channel. We'll brief on the incident call in 30m and capture remediation steps for the postmortem.
ops-bot: Incident call scheduled: today in 30 minutes — meeting INF-1125-review.
